target_customer: Lesbian, bisexual and queer women, non-binary and trans people seeking dating and community
problem: Lesbian dating sites were adapted from gay men's platforms and did not serve queer women well.
business_model: Freemium consumer app with premium subscription

founders.name: Robyn Exton
founders.background_notes: Inspired by Grindr per Wikipedia; no education or employers found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile matching and community app with standard geolocation, profiles and moderation.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity of a niche community and identity-specific trust created local network effects, though big dating apps could add similar filters.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Match Group acquired HER in May 2025, calling it its first platform focused solely on queer women.

market_need_then: Queer women were underserved by apps adapted from gay male or straight platforms, and Dattch reported half a million matches by March 2015 across the UK, Ireland and US cities.

branding.name_origin: Launched as Dattch, short for Date Catch. Renamed Her in March 2015 because people read Dattch as slurs and the founder said we are all Her.

identity.voice_and_tone: Created by and for queer folks, inclusive and community-led

branding.brand_signature: We are all Her; Pride Pins and identity labels

rebrands.why: Users read Dattch as slurs and the founder wanted the name to reflect broader inclusion

branding.community_and_virality: Claims over 15 million users and community features such as events and interest groups; featured on the Tamron Hall show in 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: A deliberate rebrand with a clear inclusive message and sustained community identity cited in press and by Match Group.

pivots.to: HER, dating and community for queer women, non-binary and trans people
pivots.why: Broaden identity inclusion and fix the name

outcome_analysis: Robyn Exton launched Dattch in 2013, renamed it HER in March 2015 with about 1 million dollars in seed money, joined YC and built a large community and premium subscription product over a decade. Match Group acquired it in May 2025. The niche focus, inclusive rebrand and community features drove durability even though funding stayed modest.
notes: The 2013 amounts: Wikipedia says 40,000 euros (March 2013) and 100,000 pounds from three investors (September 2013); the pre_seed amount is left null because the currency conversion would be guesswork and only one source was seen. Clay reports 2.4M over two rounds, unverified. TechCrunch named no competitors and the dated search found none, so the list is empty. No Series A found. Education and prior employers not found.
